---
title: "Execution Profiles and Local/Manual-HPC Handoff"
---

SCGSim uses one run-and-handoff contract. It does not define separate semantic
runners for different machines.

## Fixed handoff profiles

Profile names describe launch shape, not a site or hostname.

| Profile | Intended use | Required receipt scope |
|---|---|---|
| `direct-local` | Direct local binary; smoke, debug, mesh/config validation, and small solves | Executable identity, inputs, environment, exit state, artifacts |
| `slurm-single-node` | Single-node `sbatch`; MPI/OpenMP, scheduler lifecycle, resource receipt, and result resolution | Scheduler/job identity, resources, launch shape, artifacts, resolution state |
| `slurm-multi-node` | Multi-node / high-memory `sbatch`; production-scale runs | Scheduler/job identity, nodes/resources, launch shape, artifacts, resolution state |

Machine differences live in caller-supplied executable, setup commands,
resources, and receipts. They do not fork the run model.

## Handoff lifecycle

```text
prepare inputs -> validate -> package handoff -> execute or transfer manually
-> collect immutable results -> resolve -> report
```

External gdsfactory/cloud execution is unsupported and must never be used as a
fallback. Palace handoff scripts and AEDT execution remain explicit;
preparation never silently submits a scheduler job or opens AEDT.
